reason: VALUE/TRANSFER lens. Two parts of the idea are right. Nodes are untouched, so there is no node-multiplier artefact, and forkmid is not a closed line. The '>=1 FP on 44b6' clause is power-dead (lambda_44b6 ~0.1-0.4), and since no parameter is picked on the lab, pooling all 56 clips is fair. The claimed value does not hold up, though. (1) Metric ceiling: score = adj_edge_J + 0.1*div_J, with division J pooled (tools/official/metrics.md l.121-149). Un-forking an evaluable FP adds +0.1*J/D and un-forking a TP costs -0.1/D, so the break-even TP-loss rate is q* = k*J*FP/TP. The rider EV of +0.0005 that the idea inherits was computed at k = 14% (exp39: 6/43 FP at 4.5 um). The idea itself says x138's dose is about half that (2/62 dummy forks >= 4.5 um), so k ~0.04-0.14. Then q* is ~0.02 on public (J 0.36) and ~0.02 median on private (J 0.13-0.25). That is the same range as the fitted TP tail at 4.5 um (1.0-2.2% on exp39 coordinates, before adding the x138 head shift of 0.74 um mean and the motion of unseen embryos). A Monte Carlo over G, recall, precision, k and q gives private EV +0.00007..+0.00014 (p10 -0.0008, p90 +0.0008, P(<0) 0.27-0.32) and public EV ~+0.00005 (P(<0) 0.27, P(=0) 0.27), not +0.0005. (2) The 'powered harm test' has no power where the sign is decided. P(0 TP removed | n = 15-25 lab TP forks) is 0.60-0.74 at q = 2% (break-even) and 0.36-0.54 at q = 4%, so it catches only gross harm (q >= 8-15%). The exp39 0/23 cannot be pooled into the bound, because 4.5 um was chosen ON those 23 TP (max 3.76 um), so the '~6-7% (95%)' bound is contaminated. The lab clips are train clips (the x138 detector and edge net were trained on them), which biases the TP-mid tail low and the gate toward passing. (3) The pass probability is misstated. Gate (b) (TP mid max <= 3.8 um) is a max statistic: (1-p38)^n = 0.29-0.63 for p38 3-4.8% and n 15-25. That gate, not the FP count, binds, so P(ship) goes from ~0.08 to ~0.25-0.5, not to 0.6. (4) Net: the incremental EV of the gate change is ~0.2-0.4 x ~+0.0001, about +0.00003 private, which is invisible and not the claimed +0.0002..+0.0004. The original benefit-conditioned gate is the value-correct design, because shipping only when the lab shows a large FP removal selects the worlds where k is high enough for EV > 0. (5) Governance: the §e rules were pre-registered with the user's OK and are to be applied mechanically. Redefining 'audit E4 passed' needs the user's OK, not only a CONTEXT line, and it must come before any exp60 result is opened (none are downloaded as of 17:42 UTC).
fix: Keep a BENEFIT-conditioned gate, pooled over the 56 clips, and pre-register it (with the user's OK) before any exp60 JSON is opened: (a) 0 TP safe-division forks removed, pooled; (b) pooled removed evaluable FP >= 3 (drop the 44b6 clause, which is power-dead); (c) replace the max-margin clause with '<= 1 lab TP fork with mid in [3.8, 4.5) um'. A max statistic fails harmless riders 40-70% of the time; this version tests the same tail. (d) nodes and inserted-fork counts unchanged. Do not use exp39's 0/23 in any bound (the threshold was selected on it). If the gate fails, K3 does not ship. Its EV at x138's dose is ~+0.0001 with P(<0) ~0.3, so losing it costs nothing measurable. The slot and agent hours go further on the D1 OOF re-score of the insertion arms or the D3 DeepCenter marginal-precision test.

The gate change adds ~+0.00003 private EV (dP(ship) 0.2-0.4 x rider EV), not the claimed +0.0003 public / +0.0002..+0.0004 private. It is below any LB or rank resolution.
